result.title: PhysResponse: Probing the Physics of Video Generation with Controlled Interventions
result.comment: 11 pages. This version contains the main paper and references only. Supplementary material will be added in a later revision
result.summary: Video generation models are increasingly viewed as world simulators, which requires not only plausible motion but dynamics that respond correctly to specified physical parameters. Existing models, datasets and benchmarks, however, largely target physical plausibility, leaving this physical parameter responsiveness insufficiently explored. We introduce PhysResponse, a benchmark that measures it at two levels: scene-conditioned simulator inversion recovers the effective gravity, friction and initial speed of generated motion, and event evaluation tests outcomes near and across critical transitions. Evaluating ten image-to-video models, we find that even the lowest parameter errors exceed those of physically correct videos by over an order of magnitude, that models rarely reproduce both outcomes of a transition pair, and that the two levels expose complementary failures that visual metrics such as PSNR miss. To supply the missing training signal, we construct 72,000 simulated videos of 20 multi-object interaction types with controlled parameters; fine-tuning on them lowers parameter errors, even on held-out interaction types, and transfers to real videos and an external physics benchmark. Continued training with a numerical encoder further lowers all three errors on held-out types. PhysResponse provides a foundation for world simulators that follow physical conditions, not just appearances.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PhysResponse 基准，用场景条件下的模拟器反演从生成视频恢复有效重力、摩擦与初速度，并以临界转变事件检验十个图生视频模型的物理参数响应性，另构建 72,000 条可控参数模拟视频用于微调。
AI.relevance_reason: 由生成结果反演隐含参数、检验模型是否真遵循指定条件，可能为诊断 LVR 中视觉条件是否被内部状态保留并用于答案提供评价思路，其反演与事件判定能否迁移到 VLM 推理可供核查。
